1.note: The word translated as **Abundantly** could refer to: (1) affliction that is frequent. Alternate translation: [Often] or (2) affliction that is severe. Alternate translation: [Severely]

The pronoun **me** here signals that from here through verse 4, people of Israel are speaking together as though they are the nation of Israel. See the discussion in the introduction to this psalm to decide whether your translation will use the plural pronoun forms or keep the singular. Alternate translation: [they have afflicted us from our youth]

The pronoun **they** does not refer to a specific group of people. It refers generally to the enemies of Israel throughout its history. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate that more clearly. Alternate translation: [my enemies have afflicted me]

The psalmist is saying what he wants the people of Israel to say and inviting them to join in communal recitation. See the discussion in the introduction to Psalms about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to say. Alternate translation: [Israel should indeed say]

2.note: The psalmist uses the word **however** here to indicate a contrast between the repeated affliction described in the first half of the verse and the failure of the enemies to ultimately prevail. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in spite of that, they did not prevail against me]

3.note: The psalmist is speaking of the enemies’ oppression as if they were farmers plowing furrows on his back. The image of **the plowers plowed** upon his back and **they made long their furrows** represents severe and prolonged suffering. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [They made me suffer, like a farmer plowing a field they made deep wounds in my back]

4.note: The psalmist is speaking of the control that wicked people had over Israel as if they were **cords** binding them, and God’s deliverance as if he **cut** those cords. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he has freed me from the control of wicked people]

The psalmist is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to refer to a type of person. If your language does not use adjectives in this way, you could translate this with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those who do evil]

5.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **shame**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [May they feel disgraced]

The psalmist is using the name **Zion**, to represent the people who live in Jerusalem and worship God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those who worship God]

6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **grass of the rooftops**, or worthless weeds which grow in a thin layer of soil dry up quickly before anyone can even pull it out, so the psalmist wishes that the lives of his enemies will be insignificant and short-lived. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as insignificant and short-lived as grass on a rooftop which withers before anyone call pull it out]

7.q: שֶׁ⁠לֹּ֤א מִלֵּ֖א כַפּ֥⁠וֹ קוֹצֵ֗ר וְ⁠חִצְנ֥⁠וֹ מְעַמֵּֽר
7.note: These two phrases are continuing the comparison of the enemies to the grass from the previous verse. Both phrases describe the worthlessness of the grass: **the reaper** cannot gather a handful of it nor can **the one binding sheaves** fill his arms with it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [so insignificant that the reaper cannot harvest it, nor can the one binding sheaves gather an armful to carry]

8.q: בִּרְכַּֽת־יְהוָ֥ה אֲלֵי⁠כֶ֑ם בֵּרַ֥כְנוּ אֶ֝תְ⁠כֶ֗ם בְּ⁠שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָֽה
8.note: This is a traditional harvest blessing that workers would exchange with those passing by. The psalmist is saying that the enemies of Zion will never receive such a blessing. In your translation, use a form that people would recognize as a blessing in your language. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh make you prosper; may Yahweh bless you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **blessing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The favor of Yahweh]

Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents the person and authority of Yahweh himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by the authority of Yahweh]
